reviews.body:
At `45ee65a21157295cdc0e31825760fa497dc3537e`, I ran `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unittests/models/test_apigee_llm.py -q`: **76 passed** on Python 3.13.16. Both added tests fail against base `1daa0eca989f5f19c8081107c1d1f9767929ba6b`, confirming the reported fix. I checked the existing reviews and discussion before reviewing; there was no prior feedback. Validation used synthetic responses, without a live Apigee proxy.

**[P2] Follow the last resolved call when an ID-bearing fragment returns to an earlier slot** (`src/google/adk/models/apigee_llm.py:1331`).

The new ID lookup can return an earlier slot, but the following fragment without an ID is always assigned to `max(self.tool_call_parts)`. That is the newest allocated call, rather than the previous call promised by the helper's docstring. For example, start `call_a`, start `call_b`, receive another fragment explicitly identifying `call_a`, then receive its continuation without an ID. That continuation is labeled `call_b`, contaminating the other call's argument buffer and leaving `call_a` incomplete.

This reproduces on the exact head above:

```python
from google.adk.models.apigee_llm import ChatCompletionsResponseHandler

handler = ChatCompletionsResponseHandler()
def send(call):
    responses = list(handler.process_chunk(
        {"choices": [{"delta": {"tool_calls": [call]}}]}
    ))
    return responses[0].content.parts[0].function_call

send({"id": "call_a", "function": {"name": "weather", "arguments": '{"city": '}})
send({"id": "call_b", "function": {"name": "clock", "arguments": '{"zone": '}})
assert send({"id": "call_a", "function": {"arguments": '"Pa'}}).id == "call_a"
assert send({"function": {"arguments": 'ris"}'}}).id == "call_a"
# Fails: the last fragment has id='call_b', name='clock'.
```

Please track the most recently resolved slot, including when the ID lookup selects an existing call, and add a regression case for returning to an earlier call before an ID-less continuation. This would make the fallback follow the previous identified call consistently.

comments.body:
Thanks, good catch. The handler now remembers the slot it resolved last, including when the id lookup picks an existing slot, and a fragment without an id continues that slot instead of the highest one.

Added `test_streaming_fragment_without_id_follows_last_resolved_call`, which uses the sequence from the review (call_a, call_b, a fragment for call_a, then a fragment without an id). On the previous commit it fails with `call_b` instead of `call_a`; with the change `tests/unittests/models/test_apigee_llm.py` passes (77 tests) and pyink is clean.

This follow-up was prepared with Claude Code.

Thank you @pcbeingused333 for your contribution! 🎉

Your changes have been successfully imported and merged via Copybara in commit d563d80.

Closing this PR as the changes are now in the main branch.
